299.body: PaymentRouter now reads provider config from the standard config file instead of environment variables, so staging and prod stop drifting. __init__ still accepts overrides for tests, route() is behavior-identical, and clear() resets to file values. The deploy charts set the file path. Testing: ran the router suite with file config and with overrides.
299.title: payment-router: load provider config from file

300.body: with_retry now caps the logged payload size at 1kb. full payloads were flooding splunk. truncation noted in the log line.
300.title: checkout: cap logged payload size in with_retry

302.body: dispatch() now returns a JSON 404 with the attempted path instead of an empty body, so frontend devs stop asking whether the gateway or the app dropped the request. Route matching is unchanged. Testing: asserted the body on unknown paths across all route groups.
302.title: api-gateway: JSON 404s with path in dispatch

303.body: total_for now applies the loyalty discount before tax instead of after, matching what finance documented. line_total is unchanged and PricingService documents the order of operations in the docstring. Past orders are unaffected, this only changes new computations. Testing: added order-of-operations tests with the finance examples.
303.title: pricing: apply loyalty discount before tax

304.body: route() now supports weighted canary entries: a provider entry can carry a canary weight that only receives traffic marked canary. This lets us soak new providers with 1% of traffic without a deploy. PaymentRouter validates the weights, __init__ accepts the new shape, and clear() resets canary state. Testing: canary traffic split verified in the routing suite.
304.title: payment-router: canary weights in route

306.body: with_retry now includes the function name in every log line it emits, so filtered views per call-site finally work. Previously all lines looked identical and finding one caller's attempts meant guessing. MAX_ATTEMPTS and BASE_DELAY are untouched. Testing: asserted the function name appears in all emitted lines!!
306.title: checkout: tag with_retry logs with function name

307.body: PaymentRouter now exposes a health endpoint that reports per-provider status, which the load balancer uses to stop sending traffic to a bad instance. __init__ wires the statuses at startup and route() updates them on each outcome. Testing: flipped a provider unhealthy and watched the endpoint reflect it.
307.title: payment-router: per-provider health endpoint

308.body: place_order now validates the shipping address before charging, instead of charging first and failing on the address after. Three customers were charged for orders that then failed address validation, and each needed manual cleanup. CheckoutService returns the address error with no side effects. Testing: added charge-after-validation ordering tests.
308.title: checkout: validate address before charging in place_order

309.body: redis slowlog threshold lowered to 5ms with alerts. caught a nasty keys * from a debug session. alerted, fixed 📟
309.title: redis-cache: slowlog alerts

310.body: redis max clients raised to 20k. was 10k, hit the ceiling during the sale. dashboard updated 🌱
310.title: redis-cache: raise max clients

311.body: place_order now emits an order_placed event after a successful order so downstream consumers stop polling the order table. CheckoutService publishes with the order id and total, and handlers/place_order.py documents the payload. Polling still works for old consumers. Testing: asserted the event fires once per order with the right payload.
311.title: checkout: emit order_placed event from place_order

312.body: PaymentRouter now caches provider capability lookups for 60s instead of fetching on every route() call. The capability endpoint is slow and route latency showed it. __init__ takes the TTL as a parameter, route() behavior is otherwise identical, and clear() empties the cache for tests. Testing: asserted one fetch serves repeated routes within the TTL.
312.title: payment-router: cache provider capabilities in route

329.body: Product now carries a badges list (e.g. 'bestseller', 'new') that get_product and list_products return. The storefront was hardcoding badges by id, which broke every launch. Badges are validated against the allowed set at write time. Testing: round-trip tests plus invalid-badge rejection.
329.title: catalog: add badges to Product

330.body: dispatch() now logs the matched route and latency at debug level for every request. Debugging misrouted traffic used to need a repro; now the answer is in the logs. Volume is bounded by debug level. Testing: confirmed log shape on staging.
330.title: api-gateway: debug logging in dispatch

331.body: The payment step now explains why each method is unavailable instead of just greying it out. render_checkout reads the reason from the method metadata we already have. Shoppers stopped filing 'my card is broken' tickets for legitimately unsupported methods. Testing: covered all four unavailable-reason variants on staging.
331.title: web-frontend: explain unavailable payment methods

332.body: route() now prefers the provider with the lowest recent error rate when weights are tied, instead of picking randomly. Ties happened constantly since two providers share the same weight, and the random choice made error spikes worse. PaymentRouter tracks a rolling error window, and clear() resets it. Testing: tied-weight simulation prefers the healthier provider.
332.title: payment-router: break weight ties by error rate

333.body: minor version upgrade for the cluster. zero downtime rolling upgrade. verified replicas healthy.
333.title: postgres-main: minor version upgrade

334.body: get_product now returns the product's primary category inline instead of requiring a second call. The product page was firing two requests for every view. list_products is unchanged. Testing: asserted single-request page loads in the storefront tests.
334.title: catalog: inline primary category in get_product

335.body: login() in oauth.py now handles the user denying consent at the provider — it raises a clear consent-denied error that the frontend turns into a friendly message, instead of a generic failure. Complete login flows are untouched. Testing: denied consent at the provider on staging and confirmed the friendly message.
335.title: auth: handle denied consent in oauth login

336.body: new_cart now accepts an optional currency parameter instead of always creating USD carts. International shoppers got a USD cart that then failed at checkout when their payment method mismatched. get_cart returns the currency, and the store persists it. Default stays USD. Testing: covered default, explicit, and invalid currency.
336.title: cart: per-cart currency in new_cart

345.body: capture_payment now distinguishes provider timeouts from provider declines in the error it raises, so checkout can decide what to show the shopper. Both used to surface as the same generic error, which made declines look like outages. The payments call itself is unchanged. Testing: simulated both failure modes and asserted distinct errors.
345.title: checkout: distinguish timeouts from declines

346.body: Tokens issued for service accounts now carry the account scope, and verify_refresh_token enforces it. Service tokens could previously call user-only endpoints, which the security review flagged. Human-issued tokens are unaffected. IdentityService documents the scope semantics. Testing: added scope-enforcement tests for both token kinds.
346.title: identity-api: scope service-account tokens

347.body: IdentityService now normalizes email case before lookup, so Hana@Example.com and hana@example.com resolve to the same account. Duplicate accounts from case variants were a recurring support theme. issue_refresh_token and verify_refresh_token operate on the normalized form. Testing: added case-variant lookup tests.
347.title: identity-api: case-insensitive email lookup

348.body: AuthService.login now records the last-login timestamp on success. The security team wanted it for the dormant-account review and we had nothing. Failed logins do not update it. Testing: asserted the timestamp updates on success only.
348.title: auth: record last-login timestamp

349.body: Hello — the session endpoint was returning internal error codes that the mobile app could not map to anything. IdentityService now translates them to the public error set before responding. issue_refresh_token and verify_refresh_token internals are unchanged, only the response mapping. Testing: covered the full internal-to-public mapping table.
349.title: identity-api: map internal session errors to public codes

350.body: route() now reads the canary cookie and pins canary-marked traffic to the canary provider entry. QA can finally test a provider in prod without affecting anyone else. PaymentRouter validates the cookie value, __init__ wires it up, and clear() resets it. Regular traffic routing is unchanged. Testing: canary-cookie requests verified pinned in the routing suite.
350.title: payment-router: pin canary traffic in route

351.body: PaymentRouter logs now include the provider, latency, and outcome on every route() call at info level. Provider debugging used to start from zero. __init__ takes an optional logger and route() behavior is unchanged. Testing: asserted the three fields on success and failure.
351.title: payment-router: structured logging in route

352.body: start_refund now supports supervisor approval for refunds above the merchant threshold: the refund is created in a pending state and the notification goes out only after approval. Large refunds previously executed immediately, which finance flagged. RefundsService tracks the pending state and workflow.py drives the approval transition. Testing: covered below-threshold, above-threshold, and approval flows.
352.title: refunds: supervisor approval for large refunds
